title: Massachusetts' plan to offer postpartum screening home visits sparks online debate
text:

Retired Massachusetts judge Jack Lu said Lindsay Clancy’s defense focused on postpartum and mental health issues could become prominent after her murder case has drawn national attention.

Massachusetts is expanding a taxpayer-funded program that sends nurses into the homes of new parents after childbirth, fueling debate over the government's role in family health care.

Gov. Maura Healey recently announced plans to invest $2 million to expand the state's Welcome Family program, which offers voluntary home visits from registered nurses after the birth of a child. Healey also proposed an additional $250,000 to strengthen the Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Program for Moms, which provides mental health support to providers caring for pregnant and postpartum patients.

"Everybody in the state, when you have a baby, you're going to have a home visit within days, weeks and that will be an opportunity for a healthcare provider to make an assessment to see if you need some additional support and resources," Healey said during an interview last week on Boston Public Radio.

CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE'S 'DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD': ATTORNEY

Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey unveiled new investments aimed at expanding postpartum mental health support across the state. (David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe/Getty Images)

Healey also said the state is investing in training healthcare providers to better identify the signs of postpartum mental health conditions.

The announcement comes amid heightened public attention to postpartum mental health in Massachusetts during the high-profile trial of Lindsay Clancy, the former labor and delivery nurse accused of killing her three young children in January 2023. In a case ultimately declared a mistrial because of a deadlocked jury, Clancy's defense argued she was suffering from severe postpartum mental illness. The case has reignited debate over how postpartum mental health conditions are identified and treated.

LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS

Lindsay Clancy is on trial in Massachusetts in connection with the January 2023 deaths of her three young children. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)

State officials say the program is intended to improve maternal health outcomes by connecting families with additional support.

The announcement also sparked debate on social media, where some users questioned whether the program represented an appropriate role for government. "Doctors and pediatricians are more than capable to conduct appropriate screenings for their patients. Say no to home visits," one user wrote on X, while another called the program "creepy" and "massive government overreach."

Not everyone opposed the proposal outright. "More overreach. However, if it's an offer, and not a mandate, it could be a good thing for some young families and single moms," comedian Bob Phillips wrote on X.

During the voluntary home visits, registered nurses answer questions about newborn care and screen for postpartum mental health concerns. (Jessica Rinaldi/The Boston Globe via Getty Images))

The reaction reflects a broader national debate over how states should balance maternal mental health, taxpayer costs, individual privacy and the role government should play in supporting new families.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Massachusetts Department of Public Health and Healey's office for additional comment.
